standard.title: Representations reflect contexts
standard.description: analyse and evaluate how people, places, events and concepts are represented in texts and reflect contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students analyse how representations of people, places, events and concepts reflect their contexts (AC9E9LY01). They have not yet evaluated how those representations are constructed and what they communicate about the context.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse and evaluate how people, places, events and concepts are represented in texts and reflect contexts.

nodes.label: Analysing representations in texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how people, places, events or concepts are represented in a text, identifying specific textual choices that construct those representations.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse how at least one person, place, event or concept is represented in a text, identifying specific textual choices that construct the representation.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how a range of people, places, events and concepts are represented across a text, examining how language, visual and structural choices each contribute to the representation.
wider: Compare how stereotypes of people, places or events are constructed across a range of texts and evaluate the assumptions underlying each
Analyse representations of events and issues in First Nations Australian media, examining how representations differ from mainstream media
Compare representations of the same event from texts produced for different audiences and analyse how the intended audience shapes the representation
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to evaluate how representations reflect context — a judgement that depends on first identifying the specific textual choices that construct the representation. Without analysis, evaluation has no evidential basis.

response_modes.reason: Students tend to accept representations as natural or accurate; encountering contrasting representations of the same subject (especially First Nations Australian media versus mainstream media) makes the constructed nature of representation visible.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations Australian media analysis and cross-media representation comparison offer rich comparative work — the contrast between insider and outsider representations is genuinely enlightening for advancing students.
success_criteria: Identifies specific textual choices that construct a representation
Analyses how those choices contribute to the representation of the person, place, event or concept

nodes.label: Evaluating representations as reflections of context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate how representations in texts reflect the contexts in which they are created, making supported judgements.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate how a representation in a text reflects the context in which it was created, with a supported judgement.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate how representations across a range of texts reflect their contexts, making supported judgements about how social, cultural and historical context shapes what is represented and how.
wider: Evaluate how representations of First Nations Australians in Australian media have changed over time and assess what those changes reveal about shifting contexts
Compare representations of the same concept in texts from different countries or cultures and evaluate what each reveals about its context
Evaluate how the context of a text's production — who made it, for what purpose — shapes its representations and what is left out

response_modes.reason: Evaluating a representation as a reflection of context requires students to reason from what is shown and how, to what that reveals about the context of production — this two-step inference needs explicit support.

success_criteria: Makes a supported judgement about how a representation reflects the context of its production
Identifies at least one aspect of context (social, cultural, historical) that shapes the representation
